learning_outcomes.description: Conceptualise, research and produce audio stories and podcasts by applying a range of journalistic reporting methods.
Demonstrate competency in industry standard technical equipment and production platforms to create audio outputs.
Respond journalistically in the provision of professional content creation using reliable, creative and ethical information gathering judgements.
Critically analyse journalistic practices using relevant theories while exploring a range of audio genres, from radio news to conversational and documentary audio.
Work collaboratively in production teams to plan, produce, and critique audio journalism stories.

assessments.task_description:
Students will complete this assignment in groups assigned at the start of the course. Full details will be posted on Blackboard in Week 2.

Based on any news of the day, each group will identify and plan a news angle, write a script, and produce a short audio news package for a hypothetical local radio station. The finished story must run 30–45 seconds (target: 40 seconds) and include one soundbite or quote from a source.

The following is what is expected for this assignment:

  • Pitch: In your tutorial, pitch your story idea to the class as a group.
  • Research and sourcing: Conduct background research, identify a source, and record a quote (a group member may serve as the source if appropriate)
  • Scripting and voicing: Write the script and assign one group member to voice and record it.
  • Editing: Combine the narration and the soundbite into a single 30–45-second audio story, edited in Audition, and exported as an MP3.

 

The final story should match the format and tone of a commercial or public broadcast news bulletin. Along with the finished audio file, submit your written script.

The radio story package will be edited using Audition software.
assessments.submission_guidelines: The submission will be made via Blackboard assignments.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description:
This is an independent assignment, not undertaken in groups. Full details will be posted on Blackboard in Week 2.

This oral presentation to be undertaken during the tutorials is a critical, mandatory step toward the course's final assignment. Completing the Pitch is a prerequisite for undertaking the next assignment, Current Affairs Story.

Each student will pitch, in class, a current affairs story that one intends to pursue as one's independent project. The pitch must make the case for why the story is compelling and worth producing as audio, and must include:

  • A clear story angle or entry point — not just a topic, but the specific people, scene, or moment that will carry the story.
  • A production plan — who you intend to interview, what access you have, and what sound elements (ambient sound, tape, etc.) you plan to incorporate.
  • A short reflection on the ethical, legal, technological, or cultural considerations relevant to producing and sharing this story — for example, consent, sensitive subject matter, representation of local or community voices, or platform/distribution concerns.


Recording of Oral and Practical Assessment 

  • All presentations will be recorded for marking purposes via recording facilities available where the assessment takes place (eg. ECHO360, Zoom, camera device)  
  • Recordings will be retained by the School of Communication and Arts for at least 12 months from the release of the final grade for the course.  
  • Recordings will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed by authorised school staff for the purposes of: 
  • Moderation of marking;  
  • Provision of feedback to the student(s) recorded; and/or  
  • Re-marking following a successful re-mark application.

assessments.task_description:
Students will undertake this assignment independently and after completing the previous assignment, Pitch: Current Affairs Story. Full details will be available via Blackboard in Week 2. 

Using what they have learned this semester, each student will be required to script, source, produce and edit a short-form audio current affairs story. The audio story should be between 3-6 minutes. One should also submit the script (however, it is not necessary for the script to match the final cut if minor changes were made to the final product during the editing process).

The story should address a social issue. This could take the form of a deep dive into a personal experience, a profile, or a broader look at how a group of people responds to an event or issue. Each student should use what they have learned about storytelling and their chosen medium to draw listeners into the narrative world through insightful use of sound elements/effects. One must also incorporate at least one short interview with a source (no more than two sources total is recommended).

When submitting your story, one should suggest a potential publication venue, e.g., ABC, Vice or quality podcasts.

Students will have the opportunity to workshop their concept, script and final product in the final tutorials.
